for example, when we approve a release workflow #403 , then we should automatically create tag and then we can use it to release a new version? 

@sepo-agent /answer

comments.body:
Yes, but I’d trigger it **after the release PR is merged**, not merely when the prepare workflow/PR is approved.

For #403 specifically, `v0.3.1` already exists: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/releases/tag/v0.3.1

Current release flow is intentionally “prepare only”:
- [`agent-release-prepare.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-release-prepare.yml#L42-L62) creates/reuses a release issue, then dispatches implementation.
- [`agent-release.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-release.md#L9-L15) tells the agent to update package/changelog but not create tags or releases.
- [`versioning.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/versioning.md#L22-L38) documents that same boundary.
- [`release-version.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/release-version.ts#L16-L28) already gives us the canonical `version -> vX.Y.Z` tag mapping.

Recommended plan:

1. Keep `Agent / Release / Prepare` as the agentic PR-creation step.
2. Add a deterministic `Agent / Release / Publish` workflow, source-repo gated like prepare.
3. Trigger publish on merged release PRs, ideally identified by a release marker in the PR body plus the changed files `.agent/package.json` and `.agent/CHANGELOG.md`.
4. In a typed CLI, read `.agent/package.json`, parse the version with `parseReleaseVersion`, verify the tag does not already exist, verify the changelog has notes for that version, then create the git tag and GitHub Release.
5. Add manual `workflow_dispatch` inputs for rerun/recovery, e.g. `version`, `target_sha`, and `dry_run`.
6. Update `versioning.md` so the documented flow becomes: prepare PR -> review/approve/merge -> publish workflow creates tag/release.

Main safety point: the tag should point at the merged default-branch commit, not the PR branch head. That makes the release reproducible and avoids publishing unmerged code.

If approved, I’d implement this as a small workflow plus CLI/tests, without changing the agent release prompt to perform GitHub writes directly.
